newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition reports anti-Taleban offensive.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition reports anti-Taleban offensive.

text.p: An opposition alliance in northern Afghanistan said on Wednesday it had launched a major offensive against the dominant Taleban Islamic militia north of the capital Kabul and advanced about 10 km (six miles).
But a Pakistan-based private Afghan news service quoted Taleban sources as saying the attack in the Jabal-us-Seraj area, some 70 km (45 miles) from Kabul, had been repulsed with no loss of territory.

Alliance sources quoted by the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said forces loyal to the ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood and northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum had launched the attack on Tuesday morning.
This was the first major attack in the area since the Taleban captured Jabal-us-Seraj from alliance forces early this year, AIP said.
It quoted witnesses as saying they saw bodies of several Taleban fighters killed in the attack, while alliance sources said about 70 Taleban fighters were captured.

The report of Tuesday's attack came two days after Taleban said it had recaptured the towns of Asmar and Shegal from opposition forces on Sunday. The two towns are in the eastern province of Kunar bordering Pakistan.
Asmar had been in the hands of anti-Taleban forces since early April and Shegal since mid-April.
The Taleban have been trying to quell an uprising in Kunar province involving Kashmir Khan, a commander of the Hizb-i-Islami guerrilla faction, and disaffected tribesmen.
The militia, which seized Kabul last September, controls about three-quarters of Afghanistan.
